brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn how the gut hormone glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) helps the brain sense sugar. It includes adults with healthy weight and adults with obesity.

The main questions this trial aims to answer are:

A. Does GLP-1 cause the brain's response to sugar? B. Do lower GLP-1 levels cause a weaker brain response to sugar in adults with obesity?

Researchers will compare each participant's brain response across four test days. On these days, GLP-1 levels will be blocked, raised, or left unchanged. Sugar will be given either into the stomach or into a vein.

Participants will:

Attend 1 screening visit Visit the clinic for 4 test days Receive sugar and get an MRI scan of their brain on each test day
brief_title: Hypothalamic GLP-1 Response in Healthy Weight and Obesity

eligibility.criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

Group 1:

* Age 18-75 years
* BMI 18.5-25 kg/m²
* Normal glucose tolerance (Fasting glucose \< 5.6 mmol/L)

Group 2:

* Age and sex-matched with group 1
* BMI≥30 kg/m²
* Impaired glucose tolerance (Fasting glucose 5.6 - 6.9 mmol/L)

Exclusion Criteria:

* Diabetes mellitus type 1 or type 2, or fasting plasma glucose \> 7.0 mmol/L
* Treatment with GLP-1 receptor agonists or other GLP-1-based therapies within the past three months
* Use of medication affecting appetite, body weight, or glucose metabolism within the past three months
* Current eating disorder (anorexia nervosa, bulimia nervosa)
* Known serious chronic disease, including but not limited to:

  * Heart disease
  * Anemia (hemoglobin \<7.0 mmol/L for women, \<8.0 mmol/L for men)
  * Renal impairment (eGFR \<60 mL/min/1.73m²)
  * Hepatic impairment (ALT or AST \>3 times upper limit of normal)
* Known monogenic obesity
* Substance abuse (current or within the past year)
* Previous bariatric surgery
* Contraindications to study procedures, including:

  * Esophageal or nasal obstruction (e.g. tumors, strictures)
  * Coagulopathy
  * History of skull base trauma
  * Esophageal varices
  * Hiatal hernia
  * Claustrophobia
  * Inability to comply with MRI requirements (e.g. remaining still)
  * Presence of non-removable magnetic objects incompatible with MRI
  * Any other condition or circumstance that, in the opinion of the study physician, may compromise safe participation in the study.

Exclusion criteria for women:

* Pregnancy, breastfeeding, or wish to become pregnant during the study period
* Women of childbearing potential not using adequate contraception
* Women using hormonal contraception (oral contraceptives, progestin- containing implants or hormonal intrauterine device.)

official_title: Quantifying Hypothalamic GLP-1 Response in Healthy Weight and Obesity: A Randomized Crossover Neuroimaging Infusion Study

primary_outcomes.measure: Hypothalamic response to glucose ingestion during GLP-1 receptor blockade compared with saline
primary_outcomes.time_frame: During the MRI scan on three test days
